 2. What amino acids are restricted in maple syrup urine disease?
Th e restricted amino acids in maple syrup urine disease are
the branched-chain amino acids—leucine, isoleucine, and 
valine.
 3. What amino acid becomes essential secondary to the enzy-
matic block in PKU?
Tyrosine becomes essential secondary to the enzymatic 
block in PKU.
 4. What is periorfacial acrodermatitis, and when does it occur?
Periorfacial acrodermatitis is a disease of the skin sur-
rounding the mouth area. It may occur as a result of speciﬁ c 
osteoblasts (the bone-building cells) to stimulate new 
bone growth and increase BMD; thus, it has an anabolic 
(or tissue building) eﬀ ect on the skeleton.
 6. Describe Paget disease and its treatment.
Paget disease is a localized, progressive, often crippling
disorder of bone remodeling resulting from overactive
osteoclasts that cause rapid bone resorption followed by 
rapid formation of new bone by osteoblasts. Th e structure
of the new bone is structurally inferior, leaving the dis-
eased bone more subject to bowing, deformity, fracture, 
and poor healing following a fracture. Th e bones most

vertebral bodies, skull, and tibia. While pain (including
